title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
summary: Given a queue of n people numbered from 0 to n-1 with distinct heights, determine the number of people each can see to their right.
statement: Given a queue of n people numbered from 0 to n-1 with distinct heights, determine the number of people each can see to their right. For the i-th person, they can see the j-th person if j > i and the minimum of their heights is greater than the maximum height of all people between them.
constraints: heights has 1 through 100000 distinct positive integers, each at most 100000.
Person i sees j>i exactly when every person strictly between them is shorter than min(heights[i], heights[j]).
Return one visibility count for every original queue position.
hints: A person sees every shorter height removed from the right-side monotonic stack, plus the first remaining taller blocker.
Scan right to left, popping and counting smaller heights; if the stack remains, count its top once; then push the current height.
For each height: while taller than top, pop and increment; if nonempty increment; push height.
Each popped shorter person has no intervening survivor tall enough to block it. The first unpopped taller person is visible and blocks everything behind it.
editorial: Each popped shorter person has no intervening survivor tall enough to block it. The first unpopped taller person is visible and blocks everything behind it.

tests.explanation: The visibility counts from left to right are three, one, two, one, one, and zero.
The first person sees heights one, two, three, and ten; each shorter person sees only its next taller blocker.
